Who it’s for

THE EVERYDAY CHALLENGE

StoryReady starts
with a real need.

An unfamiliar place can bring unfamiliar people, sounds, expectations, and transitions all at once. A short, recognizable story can offer a way to talk through what may happen before arriving.

Make the sequence easier to understand while leaving room for questions, breaks, and changes.

HOW IT COULD WORK

A thoughtful path
through the moment.

This walkthrough illustrates the intended experience. It describes the product direction, not functionality available on this website.

  1. Describe the upcoming moment

    A parent could describe a dentist visit, a first day at preschool, or a trip, including what the child already knows and what needs explanation.

  2. Review and personalize the story

    Choose familiar characters, adjust the wording and sequence, and remove details that do not fit. The adult would check the story before sharing it with the child.

  3. Prepare together

    Revisit a short illustrated sequence, use a first-then view, or listen to a familiar recorded voice. Include ways to ask for help or a pause.

PLANNED CAPABILITIES

The details
we’re exploring.

  • Generate visual stories and illustrated routines from a simple description.
  • Keep child and family characters consistent across stories.
  • Prepare for preschool, doctor visits, travel, haircuts, and other transitions.
  • Explain emotions and social situations with accessible illustrations.
  • Offer visual countdowns and first-then schedules.
  • Support familiar recorded voices, multiple languages, and adaptable visual complexity.

AN EVERYDAY EXAMPLE

What support could look like.

Before a dentist visit, a family could create a short story showing the likely sequence, the people their child may meet, and how to ask for a break.

A design consideration

Families would review stories for accuracy and fit. Preparation should make room for uncertainty and a child’s choices, including asking for a pause.

ACCESSIBILITY & CONTROL

Designed around
the person using it.

Adjustable visual detail, short sequences, familiar voices, and language choices would support different communication needs without assuming that one story format works for every child.

Privacy, affordability, and user autonomy are shared Biro.dev design principles. Product-specific data practices, supported access methods, and any offline capabilities would be explained before public release.

Read our design commitments

QUESTIONS ABOUT STORYREADY

A clearer picture.

Would the story promise exactly what will happen?

No. The intended approach would distinguish likely events from details that may change, and include ways to respond when an experience differs from the story.

Could a family use it for everyday routines?

Yes, that is part of the planned direction, alongside preparation for specific upcoming events. A routine could be broken into a short illustrated sequence.

Would family photos be required?

Photo requirements and personalization methods are not finalized. The goal is recognizable characters with meaningful choices about personal information.

When can I use StoryReady?

StoryReady is in early concept development. There is no public release date, price, or supported-platform list yet. The next step is to develop and evaluate the intended experience.
